text:
ana: Quick design review — regression diff modal feels like it's asking for approval of the wrong thing. Primary CTA says "Approve" but it's ambiguous whether you're approving the run, the changes, or the whole prompt set.
jamal: Agreed. I clicked it and thought it would merge changes into the prompt set. :grimacing:
lucy: What if primary CTA said "Approve changes" and secondary "Approve as-is (no change)"? feels long though.
sam: We talked about short CTAs for mobile density. Maybe:
- Primary: "Apply changes"
- Secondary: "Keep current"
maya: hmm. "Apply" might sound too technical. Users sometimes expect "Merge" or "Save". Need to match mental model.
nana: (typo) ana: Also accessibility: keyboard order currently puts secondary first in DOM. Screen readers announce "Keep current" before the main action.
jamal: That's a bug — DOM order should match visual prominence. I'll file a tiny task.
lucy: Copy options to test in A/B:
1) "Approve changes" / "Discard changes"
2) "Apply changes" / "Keep current"
3) "Merge edits" / "Cancel"
sam: For the scorecard flow we should surface what changed inline: small tag next to each test with green/yellow/red and a hover tooltip explaining what changed.
maya: Agree. Also add an aria-live region when the diff loads: "13 tests changed, 2 regressions" — helpful for screen reader users.
design-bot: upload: /files/regression-modal-v3.png
lucy: Visual note: CTA color — darker teal for primary, neutral outline for secondary. Contrast passes with #084b4b on white?
ana: I'll run the contrast checker. Also we should reduce prominence of third-tier action "View full diff" — move it into a kebab menu so it doesn't compete.
jamal: API teams asked that the confirm CTA include which model/version it's for: e.g., "Apply changes to gpt-3.5-redwood@v2" — maybe too verbose in button.
sam: Could be a helper text under the CTA: "Applying to gpt-3.5-redwood@v2 — will update prompt set history."
lucy: Final ask: design to provide microcopy variants for the approval toast: "Changes applied" vs "Run approved" vs "Prompt set updated". We need consistent terminology across console.
maya: I'll prototype and bring screenshots tomorrow. Tagging @ana @sam for final copy sign-off.
